title: Telemetry Factory — upgrade cookbook and TF stage notes
content:
Purpose
This is a working cookbook for upgrading and consolidating telemetry stacks in private deployments (VPC + on-prem). It focuses on an auditable, staged Terraform-driven rollout for: Prometheus scraping + long-term storage, Grafana dashboards + provisioning, OpenTelemetry Collector (otelcol) pipelines, and log shipping (s3/kafka/archival).

Goals and constraints (what success looks like)
- Zero customer-visible telemetry breaks during business hours for Dedicated/Private customers.
- Upgrade path must support a canary subnet first, then region rollouts.
- Terraform-first: modules should be idempotent and support a "plan-only" dry run for safety.
- Backpressure and local disk protection for on-prem instances (avoid OOM/disk full).
- Integrate with existing KMS for encrypted archives and signed dashboard provisioning.

High-level approach
1) Prep: reconcile current TF state & inventory (list all workspaces/states).
2) Module landing: introduce new telemetry-factory TF modules in an "opt-in" namespace (tf workspace naming: telemetry-factory-<env>-<region>).
3) Canary: pick low-risk customer / dev VPC and deploy otel + prometheus sidecar + grafana-provisioning. Run for 48–72 hours.
4) Validation: smoke tests, scrape counts, otlp success rate, retention write checks.
5) Rollout waves by customer size / network topology.

Inventory / discovery checklist (notes to self)
- get list of existing prom servers: prometheus-targets.csv (from endpoint-scan)
- grafana folders: who has admin write? (do not overwrite unrelated folders)
- otel collector versions in use: 0.54.x, 0.55.x (we want to standardize on >=0.56)
- log sink types: fluentbit -> kafka, fluentd -> s3, filebeat -> graylog (legacy)

Terraform module notes (module design and variables)
- Module name: telemetry-factory/collector (root module: modules/telemetry-factory/collector)
  - variables (string): name_prefix, otel_image_tag, scrape_interval, cache_disk_gb, enable_metrics_export (bool as string: "true"/"false" for simple TF string-only fields in this doc)
  - outputs (strings): collector_service_name, otel_config_map_name, collector_version_tag
  - important behavior: set create_before_destroy = true on stateful resources where possible (PVCs).
- Module name: telemetry-factory/prometheus
  - variables: prometheus_version, retention_days, remote_write_enabled, remote_write_endpoint
  - special: expose a "remote_write_queue_config" map in TF that gets templated into prom.yaml (watch out for HCL -> YAML escaping).
- Module name: telemetry-factory/grafana-provision
  - variables: org_name, provisioning_admin_user, grafana_image_tag, default_dashboards (list)
  - behavior: only provision dashboards under a reserved folder id to avoid stomping customer folders. If folder_id == "auto" then we create a tenant-scoped folder.

Upgrade plan (step-by-step)
Stage 0 — pre-reqs (1 week)
- run `tf state list` for all TF workspaces and export list. Tag each workspace with owner and last-modified.
- snapshot all grafana provisioning config (JSON) and S3 bucket policies.
- create backup procedure for Prometheus TSDB (snapshot to s3 or local archive); test restore in dev cluster.

Stage 1 — module landing (dev + staging) (2 weeks)
- merge modules into infra-mono repo behind feature flag.
- apply to dev workspace: `telemetry-factory-dev` with minimal features: otel collector (agent), prom scrape, no remote_write.
- run basic smoke tests: scrape_count == current, new collector logs show successful scrape pipelines.

Stage 2 — canary (1 week)
- choose one canary private deployment (low traffic). Enable remote_write to staging-loki or staging-longterm to ensure remote write wiring works.
- monitor for 72 hours. Key signals: prometheus_scrape_failures == 0, otlp_export_success_rate > 99%, disk_usage < 70%.

Stage 3 — progressive rollout (2–6 weeks)
- waves: 1) horizontal small tenants, 2) mid-size with burst capacity, 3) large tenants (coordinate maintenance windows).
- at each wave: create a rollback TF plan that reinstates old module (we keep previous module as module/telemetry-legacy for quick revert).

Stage 4 — cleanup and deprecation (1 week)
- once all tenants are migrated and stable for 7 days, deprecate legacy modules and archive configs.

Rollback strategy (fast reverts)
- Keep the old collector deployment manifest (in S3 at artifacts/telemetry-legacy/<date>). If new collector misbehaves, `tf apply` to restore legacy module and restart service.
- For Prometheus TSDB corruption: mount the last snapshot into a restore cluster and verify data integrity before switching remote_write target.

Operational runbook excerpts (for on-call)
- Symptom: scrape errors spike -> check network ACLs between scrape target and prom server; verify TLS cert expiry for mTLS targets; check remote_write queue fullness.
- Symptom: otelcollector OOM loops -> check cache_disk_gb and collector queue settings. If disk pressure, scale collector to extra replica or enable disk-backed queue (see collector memory_queue config snippet below).
- Symptom: logs not arriving in S3 -> check fluentbit stdout, check bucket policy for putObject; verify KMS key grants for the gateway role.

OTel Collector (recommended pipeline snippets)
- Receivers: otlp (grpc + http), prometheus_scrape
- Processors: batch, memory_limiter, attributes (drop debug logs), resourcetotelemetry
- Exporters: prometheusremotewrite, otlp (internal long-term), file/rotate (for on-prem archival), kafka (for downstream processing)
- Important config knobs: memory_limiter: { limit_mib: 2048, spike_limit_mib: 384 } for mid-size nodes; the TF var `cache_disk_gb` must map into the file/rotate exporter directory size.

Prometheus considerations
- Use federation for central metrics only (slow queries otherwise). Avoid federating TSDB raw blocks unless necessary.
- retention_days default: 14 (can be 30 for enterprise customers with more storage).
- remote_write queue_config tuning: capacity, max_samples_per_send, batch_send_deadline. Default conservative values in module: capacity=2500, max_samples_per_send=1000, dead_line=5s.

Grafana provisioning and dashboards
- Use provisioning config to manage datasources and dashboards. Keep dashboards as JSON files in repo: dashboards/tenant-<id>/. Provision only under tenant folder id.
- RBAC: provisioning_admin_user must map to an OIDC group. Avoid hardcoding admin password in TF; integrate with Vault.

Log shipping and archival patterns
- Preferred: fluentbit -> kafka -> centralized consumer -> s3 (multipart archive) with KMS SSE-KMS.
- On-prem direct to S3 is acceptable if egress bandwidth is sufficient. Otherwise use local compressed chunking + periodic multi-part upload.
- Retention policy: hot local 7 days, cold archive 365 days (customer-configurable).

Smoke tests and validation (to automate in CI)
- scrape_count check: target count difference <= 2 from baseline.
- query_latency: 95th percentile for prom_query_range < 2s for internal dashboards.
- export_ok: otlp_export_success_rate >= 99.5% over 1h window.
- dashboard_provision: GET /api/folders/uid/<folder> returns expected dashboards.

Monitoring and SLOs to watch during rollout
- prometheus_scrape_total{job="telemetry"} failures
- otel_exporter_success_count / otel_exporter_request_count
- disk_free_bytes for collector nodes
- grafana_provision_errors (http 4xx/5xx on provisioning endpoints)

Security and IAM notes
- All S3 buckets must be encrypted with customer-managed KMS keys for private deployments; module should accept kms_key_arn variable.
- Collector <-> backend auth: prefer mTLS for internal endpoints. TF module should generate certs via CA service or accept cert ARNs.

Known risks / open questions
- Backwards compatibility of rule recording alerts with new prom version (prom recording rules may need rewrite).
- Query load: centralizing long-term storage can increase query latencies; consider query offloading.
- Grafana folder collisions if tenants have custom dashboards outside provisioning. We need a safe-namespacing approach.

Action items (owners in parens)
- inventory script to export all prom/grafana instances (Luca) — due 2025-02-21
- finalize TF module variables and docstrings (Priya) — due 2025-02-25
- prepare canary deployment plan and choose customer (Jordan + Aisha) — due 2025-02-28

Notes to self (scrappy)
- keep the legacy module around for at least 2 weeks after final cutover — easier rollback.
- test KMS rotation path early. If KMS key changes, S3 objects might be unreadable without re-encrypt step.

Appendix: sample TF variable block (copy into module README)
```
variable "name_prefix" {
  description = "prefix for resource names"
}
variable "otel_image_tag" {
  description = "otel collector image tag"
  default = "otelcol:0.56.0"
}
variable "cache_disk_gb" {
  description = "disk for file-backed exporter queues"
  default = "20"
}
```
(remember to convert defaults to proper types in TF module repo)

-- end of working draft --
